name: Packet Capture (pcap)
description: Bundled producer (docs/DESIGN-traffic-attribution.md §1, the fourth traffic class): make the packets the connection monitor structurally cannot see — nmap -sS SYN scans, masscan, UDP scans, any half-open probe that never completes a handshake — visible on the RedLog timeline. Shells out to tcpdump (needs root / CAP_NET_RAW, which RedLog itself does not hold), folds packets into flow summaries, and POSTs them to the local API as scanner.packet_flow events. Runs out-of-process — no capture code runs inside RedLog. Attribution (which command opened the flow) is added by RedLog's ingest via the source port. Remove or disable it if you don't want packet capture.
author: RedLog

capture.name: tcpdump → scanner.packet_flow
capture.description: Capture on an interface with tcpdump and land per-flow summaries (five-tuple, byte/packet counts, TCP flags, and a syn_only flag for half-open scans) on the timeline. Requires elevation.

manualSteps.label: Capture (elevated — tcpdump needs root/CAP_NET_RAW; adjust the interface)
Or keep RAW packets (rotating .pcap on your disk; only the sha256 goes on the chain)

capture.name: tshark → scanner.packet_flow (Windows)
capture.description: Windows/npcap capture via tshark, emitting the same per-flow summaries (syn_only flags half-open scans). Requires npcap + an elevated shell.

manualSteps.label: Capture (elevated — npcap needs Administrator; adjust the interface name)
